(cmd-sample_mof5)=
### Open Sample ▸ MOF-5

`sample_mof5`

Zn4O nodes and benzene-1,4-dicarboxylate linkers -- the framework every other one gets compared to.  Written in P1, so Symmetry > Find symmetry has Fm-3m to recover from it

```{index} MOF-5
```

(cmd-sample_hkust1)=
### Open Sample ▸ HKUST-1

`sample_hkust1`

Copper paddlewheels and benzene-1,3,5-tricarboxylate, in Fm-3m with six sites in the asymmetric unit -- the small end of what a whole framework can be written as

```{index} HKUST-1
```

(cmd-sample_zif8)=
### Open Sample ▸ ZIF-8

`sample_zif8`

Zinc 2-methylimidazolate: the zeolitic imidazolate framework, as a 102-atom cell with no symmetry on it

```{index} ZIF-8
```

(cmd-sample_mfu4l)=
### Open Sample ▸ MFU-4l

`sample_mfu4l`

Zn5Cl4 Kuratowski nodes and a bis(triazolyl) linker.  A 31 A cubic cell, and this project's usual stress case: what a slow operation is measured against

```{index} MFU-4l
```

(cmd-sample_ni2cl2btdd)=
### Open Sample ▸ Ni2Cl2(BTDD)

`sample_ni2cl2btdd`

Nickel-chloride chains bridged by a bis(triazolo)dioxine linker, with the solvent still in the pores.  Rhombohedral, R-3m -- a cell that is not orthogonal

```{index} Ni2Cl2(BTDD)
```

(cmd-sample_cfa1)=
### Open Sample ▸ CFA-1

`sample_cfa1`

Zn5(OAc)4(bibta)3: the Kuratowski node again, capped with acetate rather than chloride, in trigonal P321.  As deposited, so its acetate is disordered over two positions -- occupancies of 0.57 and 0.43 to look at

```{index} CFA-1
```

(cmd-sample_cfa1_p1)=
### Open Sample ▸ CFA-1 in P1

`sample_cfa1_p1`

The same framework and the same cell, modelled ordered and written out in P1: 210 atoms, two formula units, every site fully occupied and none of them related by anything

```{index} CFA-1 in P1
```

(cmd-sample_cod_mof5)=
### Open Sample ▸ From the COD ▸ MOF-5

`sample_cod_mof5`

Lock et al., J. Phys. Chem. C 2010: MOF-5 as refined, in Fm-3m with seven sites, where the one above is written out in P1

```{index} MOF-5
```

(cmd-sample_cod_hkust1)=
### Open Sample ▸ From the COD ▸ HKUST-1

`sample_cod_hkust1`

Peterson et al., Chem. Mater. 2014: Cu3(BTC)2 in Fm-3m from in-situ diffraction, with no guest in the file

```{index} HKUST-1
```

(cmd-sample_cod_zif8)=
### Open Sample ▸ From the COD ▸ ZIF-8

`sample_cod_zif8`

De Zitter et al., CrystEngComm 2024: ZIF-8 in I-43m, with each methyl hydrogen disordered over two positions

```{index} ZIF-8
```

(cmd-sample_cod_uio66)=
### Open Sample ▸ From the COD ▸ UiO-66

`sample_cod_uio66`

Oien et al., Cryst. Growth Des. 2014: UiO-66 with its defects refined -- linkers at 73 % and the cluster oxygens split over two positions

```{index} UiO-66
```

(cmd-sample_cod_mil101)=
### Open Sample ▸ From the COD ▸ MIL-101(Cr)

`sample_cod_mil101`

Lebedev et al., Chem. Mater. 2005: an 89 A cubic cell in Fd-3m, 16 000 atoms with no hydrogens, 4304 of them the oxygens of the water in its cages -- the largest thing in this menu

```{index} MIL-101(Cr)
```

(cmd-sample_cod_nu1000)=
### Open Sample ▸ From the COD ▸ NU-1000

`sample_cod_nu1000`

Islamoglu et al., CrystEngComm 2018: Zr6 nodes and a pyrene tetracarboxylate in P6/mmm, 510 atoms in the cell

`sample_cod_mil100`

Horcajada et al., Chem. Commun. 2007: Fe3O trimers and trimesate in Fd-3m, a 73 A cell of 13 552 atoms with no hydrogens -- MIL-101's smaller sibling

### Open Sample ▸ Prepared for simulation ▸ cubic-EuHOTP

(cmd-save)=
### Save File

`save` · Ctrl+S

Save the session -- the structure, the bonds you drew, the view, the selection and the measurements -- over the file this is, without asking where

```{index} Save File
```

(cmd-save_as)=
### Save As...

`save_as` · Ctrl+Shift+S

Save the session under another name

```{index} Save As...
```

(cmd-export)=
### Export...

`export`

Write a file for something else to read -- a CIF, an XYZ.  One way: it never becomes this document's file

```{index} Export...
```

(cmd-export_image)=
### Export Image...

`export_image`


(cmd-export_stl)=
### Export as STL...

`export_stl`

One unit cell with its bonds, as a mesh a 3D printer can take.  Blender does the meshing, so it has to be installed -- see Preferences > Engines

```{index} Export as STL...
```

(cmd-export_net)=
### Export Net for Systre...

`export_net`

The net drawn on this structure as a .cgd file, for Systre to name -- a second opinion on the Net panel that does not come from the code that gave the first

```{index} Export Net for Systre...
```

(cmd-save_building_block)=
### Save as a building block...

`save_building_block`

Write this molecule into the folder the MOF builder reads, so it appears in the block picker beside the 867 PORMAKE ships.  It needs connection points on it -- the dialog says what is missing.

```{index} Save as a building block...
```

## Structure

(cmd-add_atom_dialog)=
### Add atom...

`add_atom_dialog` · Ctrl+Shift+A

*No description yet.*

```{index} Add atom...
```

(cmd-add_centroid)=
### Add centroid...

`add_centroid`

Put an atom at the middle of the selected atoms -- a dummy atom, which bonds to nothing and is what net edges and measurements are drawn to, or an element

```{index} Add centroid...
```

(cmd-merge_atoms)=
### Merge atoms

`merge_atoms`

Replace the selected atoms with one at their middle -- of their element when they share one, a dummy atom when they do not.  Whole orbits go, as with Delete, and the new atom is bonded to nothing

```{index} Merge atoms
```

(cmd-add_hydrogens)=
### Add hydrogens...

`add_hydrogens`

Complete every main-group coordination with the hydrogens an X-ray structure never had

```{index} Add hydrogens...
```

(cmd-insert_molecule)=
### Insert molecule...

`insert_molecule`

Build a molecule from a SMILES string and paste it into this structure.  It arrives with the bonds the builder gave it and no others, and pasting into a group with symmetry multiplies it -- the dialog says by how much before you press the button.

```{index} Insert molecule...
```

(cmd-fill_pores)=
### Fill pores with molecules...

`fill_pores`

Put copies of a molecule -- from another tab or a file -- into the empty space of this structure, each where it touches nothing.  A host with symmetry is reduced to P1 first, and bonds are not recalculated

```{index} Fill pores with molecules...
```

(cmd-interpenetrate)=
### Interpenetrate...

`interpenetrate`

Thread copies of this framework through its own pores: every placement the lattice allows is measured, and one where atoms of two copies would meet cannot be chosen.  The copies keep their bonds, and the result is in P1

```{index} Interpenetrate...
```

(cmd-prepare_simulation)=
### Prepare for simulation...

`prepare_simulation`

Make a deposited structure one a calculation can use: order the disorder into whole atoms, remove solvent, complete M3O trimers, add the missing hydrogens and take the primitive cell -- each step saying what it chose before anything is done, and one undo step for the lot

```{index} Prepare for simulation...
```

(cmd-mark_connection_points)=
### Mark connection points

`mark_connection_points`

Turn each selected atom that has exactly one bond into a connection point: a dummy 0.75 A along that bond, which is what a PORMAKE building block is joined by.  There is no unmark -- an X does not remember what it was, so the way back is Ctrl+Z.

```{index} Mark connection points
```

(cmd-mark_one_connection_point)=
### Mark as one connection point

`mark_one_connection_point`

Collapse the selected atoms into a single connection point, 0.75 A from the middle of everything they were bonded to and carrying those bonds.  For a chelate: two atoms that meet the next block together are one joint, and marking them separately gives a block with twice the coordination number it has.

```{index} Mark as one connection point
```

(cmd-bond_rules)=
### Bond rules...

`bond_rules`

Which atoms bond, and how close they have to be

```{index} Bond rules...
```

(cmd-recompute_bonds)=
### Recalculate bonds

`recompute_bonds`

Perceive the bonds again from the geometry as it is now.  Bonds do not change on their own when atoms move; this is what changes them.

```{index} Recalculate bonds
```

(cmd-reset_bonds)=
### Reset bonds to automatic

`reset_bonds` · Ctrl+B

Drop the bonds you drew and the ones you deleted, and take what the distance criteria give.  The only way back from a deleted bond once the undo stack has gone, because a deletion is saved with the project.

```{index} Reset bonds to automatic
```

(cmd-bonds_follow)=
### Bonds follow the geometry

`bonds_follow` · toggle

Re-perceive the bonds after every edit that moves an atom, instead of only when you ask

```{index} Bonds follow the geometry
```

(cmd-measure_selection)=

`measure_selection` · Ctrl+M

(cmd-define_plane)=
### Define plane from selection

`plane_angle`

Measure the angle between the planes defined so far -- one measurement per pair

## View

(cmd-style_ball_stick)=
### Style ▸ Ball and stick

`style_ball_stick` · toggle

Atoms at half their covalent radius, tubes for bonds

```{index} Ball and stick
```

(cmd-style_ball_stick_occupancy)=
### Style ▸ Ball and stick (occupancy)

`style_ball_stick_occupancy` · toggle

Ball and stick, with every shared or partly empty site cut into wedges -- one per occupant, and a grey one for the vacancy

```{index} Ball and stick (occupancy)
```

(cmd-style_stick)=
### Style ▸ Stick

`style_stick` · toggle

Bond-width tubes with matching spheres at the joints

```{index} Stick
```

(cmd-style_wireframe)=
### Style ▸ Wireframe

`style_wireframe` · toggle

Bonds as lines, no atom geometry

```{index} Wireframe
```

(cmd-style_net)=
### Style ▸ Net only

`style_net` · toggle

The topology and nothing else -- no atoms and no chemical bonds, for looking at the net a framework reduces to

```{index} Net only
```

(cmd-style_spacefill)=
### Style ▸ Space filling

`style_spacefill` · toggle

Atoms at their van der Waals radius

```{index} Space filling
```

(cmd-style_ortep)=
### Style ▸ Thermal ellipsoids (ORTEP)

`style_ortep` · toggle

Atoms as displacement ellipsoids at the probability level set in the style panel -- the picture that makes a bad refinement obvious

```{index} Thermal ellipsoids (ORTEP)
```

(cmd-style_polyhedra_stick)=
### Style ▸ Polyhedra and sticks

`style_polyhedra_stick` · toggle

Coordination polyhedra for the nodes and tubes for everything else -- an MOF's metals and its linkers in the same picture

```{index} Polyhedra and sticks
```

(cmd-style_polyhedra)=
### Style ▸ Polyhedra

`style_polyhedra` · toggle

Coordination polyhedra as translucent hulls, coloured by the atom at the centre

```{index} Polyhedra
```

(cmd-style_platon)=
### Style ▸ Ellipsoid plot (PLATON)

`style_platon` · toggle

The ellipsoid plot a structure report is checked in: pale outlined atoms, thin dark bonds and no highlight -- what PLATON and checkCIF draw

```{index} Ellipsoid plot (PLATON)
```

(cmd-style_cartoon)=
### Style ▸ Cartoon

`style_cartoon` · toggle

Flat colour inside a dark outline, and no shading at all -- the one style that exports as plain circles and strokes an illustrator can recolour

```{index} Cartoon
```

(cmd-show_atoms)=
### Show ▸ Atoms

`show_atoms` · toggle

*No description yet.*

```{index} Atoms
```

(cmd-show_bonds)=
### Show ▸ Bonds

`show_bonds` · toggle

*No description yet.*

```{index} Bonds
```

(cmd-show_bond_orders)=
### Show ▸ Bond orders

`show_bond_orders` · toggle

Draw a double bond as two tubes and a triple as three, with an inner dashed line for an aromatic one

```{index} Bond orders
```

(cmd-show_topology)=
### Show ▸ Net (topology bonds)

`show_topology` · toggle

Draw the net a chemist marked out over the framework -- thicker and translucent, over the real bonds rather than in place of them

```{index} Net (topology bonds)
```

(cmd-show_cell)=
### Show ▸ Unit cell

`show_cell` · toggle

*No description yet.*

```{index} Unit cell
```

(cmd-show_axes)=
### Show ▸ Cell axes (a, b, c)

`show_axes` · toggle

The triad in the corner of the view: which way a, b and c point as the structure turns

```{index} Cell axes (a, b, c)
```

(cmd-show_planes)=
### Show ▸ Planes

`show_planes` · toggle

Draw a translucent quad at every plane in the Measure panel, with its normal on it -- choose rows in that list to draw only those

```{index} Planes
```

(cmd-show_pores)=
### Show ▸ Pore network

`show_pores` · toggle

Draw what a porosity run found: the largest pore where it sits, and the channels it belongs to.  Nothing is drawn until Modules > Zeo++ has answered

```{index} Pore network
```

(cmd-labels)=
### Show ▸ Labels

`labels` · toggle

*No description yet.*

```{index} Labels
```

(cmd-show_legend)=
### Show ▸ Element legend

`show_legend` · toggle

*No description yet.*

```{index} Element legend
```

(cmd-show_scale_bar)=
### Show ▸ Scale bar

`show_scale_bar` · toggle

A ruler in the corner, in Angstrom.  It measures the camera and not the crystal, so a cell that contracts during a relaxation is seen to contract against it

```{index} Scale bar
```

(cmd-clear_overlays)=
### Clear charges and orbital

`clear_overlays`

Take a DFTB+ run's atom colouring and orbital lobes off the picture.  They go by themselves when the atoms move

```{index} Clear charges and orbital
```

(cmd-display_range)=
### Display range...

`display_range` · Ctrl+R

How much of the crystal to draw

```{index} Display range...
```

(cmd-boundary_in_range)=
### Bonds at the boundary ▸ Drop bonds at the boundary

`boundary_in_range` · toggle

A bond whose far atom is outside the range is not drawn, so every atom on the surface of the picture is drawn under-coordinated

```{index} Drop bonds at the boundary
```

(cmd-boundary_bonded)=
### Bonds at the boundary ▸ Complete bonds at the boundary

`boundary_bonded` · toggle

Draw the far atom as well.  The only way a coordination polyhedron at the cell edge stays whole, at the cost of a halo of extra atoms around the box

```{index} Complete bonds at the boundary
```

(cmd-boundary_half)=
### Bonds at the boundary ▸ Draw half bonds at the boundary

`boundary_half` · toggle

Draw the near half and nothing on the end of it -- the usual notation for a bond that leaves the picture, and the only one that draws a six-coordinate net vertex with six edges

```{index} Draw half bonds at the boundary
```

(cmd-orthographic)=
### Orthographic projection

`orthographic` · toggle

*No description yet.*

```{index} Orthographic projection
```

(cmd-depth_cue)=
### Depth cueing

`depth_cue` · toggle

Fade distant atoms towards the background, so a thick slab reads as having depth instead of as a flat mat of spheres

```{index} Depth cueing
```

(cmd-view_a)=
### Along a

`view_a` · 1

Look down the a axis

```{index} Along a
```

(cmd-view_b)=
### Along b

`view_b` · 2

Look down the b axis

```{index} Along b
```

(cmd-view_c)=
### Along c

`view_c` · 3

Look down the c axis

```{index} Along c
```

(cmd-reset_view)=
### Reset view

`reset_view` · Ctrl+0

Frame the whole of what is drawn again

```{index} Reset view
```

## Modules

(cmd-show_ff)=
### Forcefield ▸ Force Field panel

`show_ff`

Atom types, electrostatics, and how the run is going

```{index} Force Field panel
```

(cmd-single_point)=
### Forcefield ▸ Single point energy

`single_point` · Ctrl+E

Energy and per-term breakdown at this geometry

```{index} Single point energy
```

(cmd-optimize)=
### Forcefield ▸ Optimise geometry

`optimize` · Ctrl+Shift+E

Relax the structure within its space group

```{index} Optimise geometry
```

(cmd-show_dftb)=
### DFTB+ ▸ DFTB+ panel

`show_dftb`

Hamiltonian, parameter set, dispersion, and how the run is going

```{index} DFTB+ panel
```

(cmd-dftb_single_point)=
### DFTB+ ▸ DFTB+: Single point energy

`dftb_single_point`

Energy and per-term breakdown at this geometry, through DFTB+

```{index} DFTB+: Single point energy
```

(cmd-dftb_optimize)=
### DFTB+ ▸ DFTB+: Optimise geometry

`dftb_optimize`

Relax the structure within its space group, through DFTB+

```{index} DFTB+: Optimise geometry
```

(cmd-module.dftb.band-structure)=
### DFTB+ ▸ Band structure...

`module.dftb.band-structure`

Eigenvalues along a path through the Brillouin zone, from charges converged on a mesh

```{index} Band structure...
```

(cmd-module.dftb.dos)=
### DFTB+ ▸ Density of states...

`module.dftb.dos`

Total and projected onto each element, on a dense mesh

```{index} Density of states...
```

(cmd-module.dftb.charges)=
### DFTB+ ▸ Mulliken charges

`module.dftb.charges`

A charge on every atom, and the atoms coloured by it

```{index} Mulliken charges
```

(cmd-module.dftb.orbital)=
### DFTB+ ▸ Orbital...

`module.dftb.orbital`

waveplot is not installed, or not on PATH (XTAL_WAVEPLOT is not set).  It is at https://dftbplus.org (it ships with DFTB+)

```{index} Orbital...
```

(cmd-module.dftb.relax)=
### DFTB+ ▸ Optimise with DFTB+'s driver...

`module.dftb.relax`

One DFTB+ run relaxes the atoms, and the cell if asked; the answer is mapped back onto the space group

```{index} Optimise with DFTB+'s driver...
```

(cmd-module.dftb.modes)=
### DFTB+ ▸ Vibrational modes...

`module.dftb.modes`

modes is not installed, or not on PATH (XTAL_MODES is not set).  It is at https://dftbplus.org (it ships with DFTB+)

```{index} Vibrational modes...
```

(cmd-module.dftb.md)=
### DFTB+ ▸ Molecular dynamics...

`module.dftb.md`

Velocity Verlet, with a thermostat; the frames go to the transport bar

```{index} Molecular dynamics...
```

(cmd-module.zeopp.diameters)=
### Porosity ▸ Pore diameters and channels...

`module.zeopp.diameters`

Zeo++ is not installed, or not on PATH (XTAL_ZEOPP is not set).  It is at https://www.zeoplusplus.org/

```{index} Pore diameters and channels...
```

(cmd-module.zeopp.surface-area)=
### Porosity ▸ Surface area...

`module.zeopp.surface-area`

Zeo++ is not installed, or not on PATH (XTAL_ZEOPP is not set).  It is at https://www.zeoplusplus.org/

```{index} Surface area...
```

(cmd-module.zeopp.surface-area-grid)=
### Porosity ▸ Surface area (faster)...

`module.zeopp.surface-area-grid`

The same area in a second or two rather than several: sampled here on this application's own grid instead of by Zeo++, which it need not have.  A window within a grid step of the probe's size is flagged rather than guessed.

```{index} Surface area (faster)...
```

(cmd-module.zeopp.volume)=
### Porosity ▸ Accessible volume...

`module.zeopp.volume`

Zeo++ is not installed, or not on PATH (XTAL_ZEOPP is not set).  It is at https://www.zeoplusplus.org/

```{index} Accessible volume...
```

(cmd-module.zeopp.volume-grid)=
### Porosity ▸ Accessible volume (faster)...

`module.zeopp.volume-grid`

The same volume in a second or two -- MFU-4l's occupiable volume is 1.7 s here against 71 s in Zeo++ -- read off this application's own grid.  A window within a grid step of the probe's size is flagged rather than guessed.

```{index} Accessible volume (faster)...
```

(cmd-module.zeopp.psd)=
### Porosity ▸ Pore size distribution...

`module.zeopp.psd`

Zeo++ is not installed, or not on PATH (XTAL_ZEOPP is not set).  It is at https://www.zeoplusplus.org/

```{index} Pore size distribution...
```

## Elsewhere

(cmd-cancel_gesture)=
### Cancel the current gesture

`cancel_gesture` · Esc

Put down a half-finished click gesture -- an add-atom chain, the first end of a bond, the atoms of a measurement.  Again to leave the mode.

```{index} Cancel the current gesture
```

(cmd-workspace_open)=
### Open

`workspace_open`

Open what is selected in the Workspace panel -- the same as double-clicking it.

```{index} Open
```

(cmd-workspace_reveal)=
### Reveal in Finder

`workspace_reveal`

Show the selected file or run folder in the desktop's own file browser.

```{index} Reveal in Finder
```

(cmd-workspace_copy_path)=
### Copy Path

`workspace_copy_path`

Put the full path of what is selected on the clipboard, for a script or a terminal.

```{index} Copy Path
```

(cmd-workspace_trash)=
### Move to Trash

`workspace_trash`

Put a run's folder in the desktop's wastebasket.  Only a run: the structure it was run on stays, and nothing here is ever deleted outright.

```{index} Move to Trash
```
